answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may place jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task fails independent verification. One person can still create many accounts, but each must lock real capital, and coordinated identities risk losing it; raising the cost per identity makes large Sybil swarms expensive rather than merely tedious. For example, a nectar seller in a meadow might escrow tokens, while a relic’s verified provenance earns release of the stake.
